BiblicalUsage: This is the word for a prisoner — one bound, one shut up. Joseph is put 'into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound'; Isaiah promises the Servant will 'bring out the prisoners from the prison'; and Lamentations says God does not delight in crushing 'all the prisoners of the earth' under His feet.
TheologicalSignificance: Joseph the prisoner becomes the keeper of the prisoners, and Isaiah promises a Servant who will open the prison doors. I believe the word runs straight to Christ: the prisoners of the earth are not forgotten by God, and the One who was bound sets the bound free.
